questions.question: A 3D asset pipeline first generates consistent views, then fits a 3D representation. What is this overall strategy?
options: A GAN discriminator converts images into camera poses
Single-view pixel classification followed by upscaling
A text encoder directly emits every mesh vertex
Multi-view generation followed by 3D reconstruction
questions.explanation: The pipeline first generates multiple views of one object, then fits a 3D representation such as Gaussian splats to those views. A text encoder can condition generation but is not the reconstruction stage that emits mesh vertices.

questions.question: How does 3D Gaussian Splatting render a scene in the lesson?
options: Project Gaussians and alpha-composite them
March rays through an MLP at every sample
Apply a mesh classifier to each camera ray
Decode a voxel grid with a transformer
questions.explanation: 3D Gaussian Splatting projects Gaussian primitives into the image plane and composites them in depth order to render a view. NeRF instead evaluates an MLP along rays to obtain color and density.

questions.question: What does a NeRF MLP predict from position and view direction?
options: A mesh face and texture coordinate
Color and density for ray integration
A Gaussian position and covariance
A camera pose and frame timestamp
questions.explanation: A NeRF MLP takes 3D position and view direction and predicts color plus density; rendering integrates those quantities along camera rays. Gaussian splatting directly represents and projects Gaussian primitives instead.

questions.question: Why can independently generated object views produce a blurry 3D reconstruction?
options: The VAE decoder cannot output RGB images
The Gaussian splat renderer requires a text prompt
Their geometry may disagree across views
The mesh topology is fixed before view generation
questions.explanation: If separate views imply different geometry, the reconstruction cannot fit one coherent object and becomes blurry or inconsistent. Shared multi-view conditioning makes the generated views agree before the 3D fitting stage.

questions.question: A product must reconstruct a scene from a set of captured photos and support real-time viewing. Which representation is the lesson’s fit?
options: A dense voxel grid for the full scene
A CLIP embedding across the captured views
A NeRF with per-ray MLP evaluation
A 3D Gaussian splatting scene representation
questions.explanation: The lesson recommends 3D Gaussian Splatting for reconstructing scenes from photos and notes its fast rendering. NeRF requires many per-ray MLP evaluations, while a CLIP embedding is not itself a renderable scene.

questions.question: A single photo is used to create a full 3D object. Which uncertainty should the pipeline account for?
options: The visible image has no camera information
The reconstruction has no dependence on training data
The model cannot represent surface color
The unseen side must be hallucinated
questions.explanation: A single photo shows only one side of an object, leaving the unseen geometry underdetermined. The pipeline must infer or hallucinate that back side, so its quality can vary.
